verdicts.strongest_argument: The claim's central assertion is factually false against its own corpus. The hunter writes: 'not one of the roughly ninety captured documents puts "margins matter more than AI orders" next to "networking is 30% of revenue and over half of profits"'. But snapshots/20260830T151804Z.json - admissible, three days before an amc print - carries, within sixty lines of each other, the margin-pressure copy ('Dell, IBM and HPE have to operate on single digit margins when it comes to the server market', techradar; 'HPE Stock: Margin Pressure Builds as AI Infrastructure Boom Accelerates', parameter.io) AND exactly the offsetting mix argument the finding claims is unmade: 'HPE earnings preview: Juniper makes networking the AI story' (techi.com, an explicit earnings preview), 'Lenovo Doubles Infrastructure Revenue, Lifting HPE 8%: Juniper Makes It More Than AI Server Rally' (techtimes, 2026-08-13), and 'HPE Stock Ticks Up: CEO Says Networking Segment "More Insulated" From Memory Supply Squeeze' - the last being the company's own CEO making the insulation-from-margin-pressure case on the record. snapshots/20260901T153853Z.json separately carries 'HPE: AI drives compute and networking revenues higher while storage languishes' and the 247wallst segment piece itself. So the arbitrage is not an arbitrage; it is the pre-print preview consensus in the captured wire copy. Compounding this: the source document is dated 2026-03-10, six months before the print, so the segment split is not a fresh datum; the '$1.7-1.9bn AI networking orders and raised EPS outlook' is company guidance issued 2026-06-01 and reported on Seeking Alpha, on which the stock moved +19.47% - the single largest reaction in the eight-event history; and the three peer datapoints (SMCI 2026-08-12, Cisco, Dell 2026-09-01) are all mainstream wire, with the hunter itself noting HPE traded up 3% on the SMCI day. What is left is the tape argument - 'if it were priced HPE would not have given back its 52-week high' - which is precisely the substitution of a run-down for an option chain that I am not permitted to accept in the other direction and will not accept here. HPE is a $72bn company with 17.8m shares a day of volume and roughly ninety captured documents; it is the least plausible name on this list to carry an unpublished synthesis.

prior_publication.what_it_says: An HPE earnings preview whose headline is that Juniper makes networking the AI story - the finding's own thesis, published as preview copy.
Explicitly argues HPE is 'more than an AI server rally' because of Juniper, i.e. connects the networking mix to the server-margin narrative, twenty days before the print.
The segment-split datum the finding is built on, published six months before the print and still indexed in the pre-print sweep.
HPE's own AI-networking order target and raised EPS outlook - published guidance, given on the June call.
The margin-framing piece the finding treats as the consensus bear case - published, and by the hunter's own account the run-in's framing piece.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The AI-networking order guidance was priced in a measured event: the 2026-06-01 amc print moved +19.47%, versus a 6.70% eight-event median. Into this print run_up_5d is -6.16% and run_up_20d -2.61% with the stock 13.36% off its 52-week high, but I explicitly decline to read that drawdown as evidence the mix argument is unpriced - that is the run-up-as-implied-move substitution, and no options anchor exists here (skew and implied move are null). The 2026-09-02 close of 51.83 is pre-print for an amc name and is admissible; note the hunter quotes a $50.49 intraday rather than the close.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A quantified pre-print consensus for HPE networking operating profit that sat materially below what the $1.7-1.9bn order guide implies, showing the mix benefit was in the narrative but not in the numbers analysts published.

interactions: The finding's own independence note is internally two-sided on the same axis - a bullish unusual-options-volume piece (barchart) and a rising-short-interest piece (Yahoo), both published, which is a description of a contested tape rather than of missed information.
